📈 **Mon 9 Nov: 1 setup** (from 6 Nov close). 3 of 455 stocks passed; 2 skipped by the checks. Valid 9 Nov, 11 Nov, 12 Nov (10 Nov is a Diwali holiday).

**💡 Today's learning:** "A crossed-out “Was” price means a real discount"
- 🤔 **What people believe:** A tag that says “Was ₹2,000, now ₹999” proves you are saving ₹1,001.
- 🔬 **The fact:** The US regulator FTC wrote its Guides Against Deceptive Pricing back in 1967: a “former price” must be the real price the item was openly sold at for a reasonably long time. Its own example: a pen marked up to $10 for a few days, then sold as “Were $10, Now Only $7.50”, is “obviously a false claim”.
- 🎯 **How they fool you:** The crossed-out number is an anchor: your brain compares against it, not against what the item is really worth. The seller wins when the “was” price was never really charged. In festive sales, check the price history or compare shops, not the strike-through.
- Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-233
